Subject: Latency spikes and 500s on /v1/generate — urgent

Hi team,

Over the past 18 hours we've seen recurring p99 spikes up to 7.2s (baseline ~350ms) and a correlated increase in 5xx responses for our production calls to your hosted endpoint (model:redwood-small-2). We attached a zipped collection of traces and a short HAR from a failing request. The pattern looks like requests are queued before a big jump in latency and then a cluster of 503/504 errors. Our users are seeing timeouts.

Can you confirm whether this is caused by model-side slowdowns, routing, or per-tenant concurrency caps? This is impacting our telemedicine workflows — high priority.

Attachments: sentinel-traces.zip (zip, ~2.2MB)

Alex — thanks for the signal and the traces. I've opened INF-4821 and attached it to this thread. Short answer: we see the same spikes on our side with queue depth amplification at the GPU pool level.

Immediate next steps (what we'll do in the next 90 minutes):
- Spin up a temporary extra worker pool in us-west to relieve the affected shard and route your traffic there (low-risk).
- Temporarily raise per-tenant concurrency cap for your account while we investigate the root cause.
- Run a quick canary against your traffic pattern to verify tail behavior is reduced.

Can you hold an immediate 30m call at 10:00 PT so we can align on mitigation and timeline? Priya, Alex's infra lead, is on the cc.

I'll loop in Marcus to share initial infra traces and recommended rollback/playbook.

—Nikhil

Internal: escalation — Sentinel Health is experiencing sustained long-tail latency and 5xx amplification. See attached traces from customer. Initial ask: 30m sync at 10:00 PT. Please prioritize.

What I need from each of you for the call:
- Marcus: initial infra signal and whether the affected GPU shard is backpressured or whether kernel stalls appear. If you can, bring a flamegraph and token-level latencies.
- Grace: timeline for customer comms and whether we should offer a short SLA credit preemptively.
- Evelyn: figure out whether any recent model build or config change could have changed decode latency distribution (quantization path, kernel swap).

Flags: traffic profile indicates a ~3x increase in short burst traffic (50–200rps bursts) from Sentinel between 01:40–03:00 PT which correlates with the first spike cluster.

Thanks — Nikhil
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Latency spikes and 500s on /v1/generate — urgent

Quick findings from the infra side after 10:00 triage: 
- The affected pool (gw-usw-2) shows sustained queue growth at the RPC frontend during the burst windows. KV-cache hit rate is normal.
- We see per-tenant concurrency cap for Sentinel set at 32 concurrent requests; during the bursts the client hit the cap and additional requests were backpressured into the global queue. The queueing, combined with a small percentage (~2%) of long-running decodes on that shard, amplified p99.
- The 5xx spike correlates with transient worker OOMs on two nodes that then restarted; the restart decision is tied to our safety circuit which triggers on sustained decode timeouts and then returns 503 for queued inflight requests.

Attachments: queue-flamegraph.png (PNG), infra-sample.log (text)

Short mitigation applied at 10:05 PT:
- Increased sentinel tenant concurrency cap from 32 -> 64 for the next 60 minutes.
- Drained two suspect workers and added 3 temporary warm instances in us-west.
- Toggled a safe decode-timeout extension for the affected model variant to reduce false-positive OOM restarts.

Early result: p99 dropped from ~7.2s to ~1.1s in the canary sample. Still monitoring for recurrence.

Next actions I recommend:
1) Run a small replay of their burst profile against the new pool to validate tail under load.
2) Investigate root cause of the long-running decodes (possible kernel change or QoS regression).
3) Consider automatic pre-warming or token-level early abort policy for heavy tail requests.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive brief & customer-facing plan — Sentinel Health latency incident

Summary for execs and customer: 
- Impact: Sentinel experienced intermittent p99 latency spikes and a small wave of 5xx responses tied to queue amplification when their burst traffic hit per-tenant concurrency caps while a small fraction of long-decode requests were active on the same shard. Customer-visible p99 peaked at ~7.2s; after mitigations p99 stabilized ~1.1s.
- Root cause hypothesis: concurrency cap hit + backpressure into global queue + isolated long-running decodes caused cascading restarts (safety circuit).

Customer-facing actions (we will communicate today):
- Explain the cause and outline the immediate mitigation we applied (extra pool, raised cap, drained/replaced workers).
- Offer a 10% credit for the affected window (Grace — please draft the credit).
- Commit to a post-mortem within 72 hours with replay results and preventive changes.

Operational next steps (internal):
- Evelyn: deep analysis on the long-run decode samples and model runtime changes (48 hours).
- Marcus: run burst-replay in staging and report tail distribution (24 hours).
- SRE/Runtime: propose a short-term autoprewarm/pre-warm policy scoped to accounts that exhibit bursty traffic (proposal in 7 days).

Escalation/visibility: I recommend we notify the Execs (CTO, Head of Product) given the potential SLA exposure and because this customer is mid-enterprise with expansion motion (deal_3429).

Call notes & links:
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821
- Slack: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02INCIDENTS/p1646421
- Attachments provided to customer: mitigation-playbook.md, queue-flamegraph.png

Planning ask: Grace — can you own customer comms and credit? Marcus/Evelyn — own technical RCA and replay. I'll coordinate exec briefing.

—Nikhil
Head of Customer Reliability

2) If you plan to change per-tenant caps or pre-warm behavior for us, we need at least 48h notice or a rolling approach that doesn't surprise our rate-limiting measures.

We'll join the post-mortem and can share a synthetic traffic generator to help with replay if useful.
